_comment: IAW 5AM live-data map. Channel names are joined to their rli by the local channel id. Cylinders labelled F/R per the V-twin layout; this engine's V-angle is 87 degrees, so the firing interval is uneven (87/633) and no per-cylinder pair should be expected to sit a fixed 90 apart. Response '61 <rli> <value>', offset 2, big-endian; length per rli from the 2026-08-18 scan. Two flags, two jobs: 'group' says which list the UI draws the row in -- 'known' = proven on this bike, 'check' = named but still to be proven there, 'unknown' = no meaning yet -- while 'default' says what a device with no selected.json polls out of the box. The 2026-09-04 stationary session moved five channels into 'known': 0x39 is the injection period at raw/1000 ms (0 with the engine off, 8.6 ms cranking, 1.89 ms at 36 C), 0x60 is barometric (962 flat, engine on or off), and 0x76/0x78/0x61 are the side stand, the clutch and the neutral flag -- the clutch polarity in status_maps.json had to be swapped, the bike answers 0 with the lever pulled. The 10-minute ride that followed confirmed the lambda integrator's scale 0.1 (-14.4..+16.9 % with 48 zero crossings) and the mV reading of 0x45 (181 crossings of 450 mV), and re-confirmed all three switch polarities from the opposite state -- riding means gear engaged, stand up, lever released. There is no gear number on this ECU: 0x61 is a neutral flag, the 5AM label page has no Value_35 ("Gear") slot, and 0x58 -- the one candidate -- turned out to be the engine-state bitfield instead. 0x37 stays open: while running it tracks 0x35 to 0.21 deg, so it is a second advance channel in tenths of a degree, but whether it is the other cylinder or a programmed-advance channel takes a decel/cut-off run to tell -- it reads a flat 8.0 deg with the engine off, which suits 'programmed'. This bike has one lambda sensor, on the front cylinder: the rear is not fitted, so 0x46, 0x48, 0x4A and 0x4C read a flat 0 here and cannot be confirmed on this machine at all -- the names are provisional and the F/R pairing is by rli order. 0x54/0x55 keep the channel but not the word 'angle': across 424 samples the pair settles after every start (869->700 in five seconds from cold, the same from a 40 C and an 87 C start, 1210 while the starter turns) and ignores rpm, which is a charge time compensated for battery voltage, not an angle -- the unit stays raw until a session with vbat and a switched load names it. The 2026-09-05 pair of sessions settled four more. 0x54/0x55 are a charge time compensated for battery voltage: inside a narrow rpm band dwell_f falls monotonically as vbat rises (1200-1600 rpm: 739 at 13.7 V, 737 at 13.8, 723 at 13.9; 2200-3000 rpm: 797 at 13.4, 778 at 13.5, 766 at 13.6), the slope is -80..-150 counts per volt, cranking at 11.2 V reads 1066/2620 and the engine off at 12.3 V a static 731/846, while rpm at a fixed voltage moves it by only ~15 counts per 600 rpm. The unit stays raw -- the count could be ~4 us (2.8 ms at 13.7 V, 4.3 ms cranking) but nothing in the log names the multiplier. 0x6B is the temperature-scheduled base position of the idle stepper: 117 at 51 C, 113 at 60, 108 at 65, 103 at 70, 100 from 75 C up, with idle_target riding along 1472 -> 1404 rpm. 0x49 is the loop flag it was named for: 2 on 3562 samples (lambda swinging about 455 mV), 0 on 947 at small throttle and on the overrun (591 mV mean). 0x58 is confirmed as the engine-state bitfield, but the labels shipped in status_maps.json were wrong and are rewritten there. The 2026-09-08 session -- two real cold starts (22 C in the morning, 27 C in the evening) and two kill-switch stops on a running engine, 2320 samples -- closed three more. 0x37 is the *live* advance, not the second cylinder: while running it is the same number as 0x35 (mean +0.02 deg over 1365 samples, and 17 % of the scatter is read skew -- r = -0.416 against the local slope of 0x35, which is read one request earlier -- while the residual is white noise, lag-1 autocorrelation 0.05, so there is no standing per-cylinder offset). The two part company only off the engine: 0x37 falls to a fixed 8.0 deg while 0x35 freezes at whatever it last held (21.0), and it does so in the very sample where inj_period, lambda_int_f, lambda_reg_f and lambda_ctl_f all reset -- 0x37 belongs to that live group, 0x35 is a latch. Cranking shows the same thing from the other side: 8.0 -> 13.0 -> 22.2 on 0x37 while 0x35 still reads 0. 0x4B is the lambda controller's phase code, split by the sign of the 0x47 step inside an unchanged state: 7 rises 266 times against 32 (lambda median 175 mV, lean) and 5 falls 200 against 35 (median 727 mV, rich), both with 0x49 = 2, so they are the two branches of the closed loop (231 and 228 transitions between them); 4 is open loop with the integrator held (57 of 120 steps flat), 1 is the controller frozen with the engine stopped (124 of 125 flat) and 2 only appears on a cold sensor (39-63 mV). Labels are in status_maps.json as 'lambda_ctl'. 0x6D is the closed-loop trim riding on top of 0x6B: from cold it ran 16 -> 36 -> 51 -> 63 -> 70 in four seconds while rpm sat 200 below idle_target and backed off (65 -> 61 -> 59) in the first sample rpm went over it; the mean step against rpm minus idle_target is monotone (-300..-201 -> +2.88, -200..-101 -> +0.92, -100..-1 -> +0.13, 0..+99 -> -0.27) and warm, with 0x6B pinned at 100, it sits 6..18. Range this session 0..73. The 2026-09-08 firmware read settled which rli can ever say anything. my_original_fw.bin holds the dispatch table for service 21 <rli> at file offset 0x045BE: 79 records of 6 bytes, {rli:u16, slot:u16, 0x0002}, running 0x30..0x7F with 0x4F missing -- the one rli that does not answer -- and 79 is what the toolchain's own comment a page later calls it ('Array di 79 bytes + 1 a disposizione per commenti'). Three slots are shared: 0x18CE by 18 rli that answer a 2-byte zero, 0x18BC by 18 that answer a 1-byte zero and 0x18EC by the two 3-byte ones. Those 38 are a constant zero by construction -- there is no code behind them -- which is why 0x3B stayed flat over 1143 samples, 0x72 over ~5600 and the whole rear bank over every ride. The table is byte-identical in 23ECCLGPSMD, so this is a property of the 5AM software, not of a calibration, and no firmware in hand changes it. 34 of them carry 'dead': true and a (null) suffix: the record stays because the rli is real, but nothing may select one -- see ParamMap.selectable(). The rear bank (0x46/0x48/0x4A/0x4C) is the deliberate exception: it is a stub *here*, and the sensor is not fitted here, but other Granpasso builds wire it, so the four keep their names and sit in 'check' with default false. 0x3D has a slot of its own (0x1AA0), so its zero is a value and not a stub -- the CO Trimm reading stays open. The 9 unknown rli that answered non-zero also have slots of their own and moved to 'check': 0x3E, 0x57, 0x5C, 0x62, 0x6C, 0x74, 0x75, 0x77, 0x7A. Two hints came free from the table order. 0x6C sits between 0x6B and 0x6D and read 164 where those two read 118 and 46 -- exactly their sum -- which reads as the idle stepper's total position (one sample, so the name carries a question mark). And 0x74/0x75/0x77/0x79/0x7A bracket 0x76 (side stand) and 0x78 (clutch), so that run is the digital-input block; each is a switch to be found by working the handlebars with the ignition on. Six unknown rli have a slot of their own and no meaning yet -- 0x5D, 0x5E, 0x5F, 0x63, 0x6E, 0x70 -- and the first four held a flat zero through the rev limiter, full throttle and a warm-up to 97 C, so what moves them is still unknown. The 2026-09-09 evening pass gave the settled channels real keys: a key is what the decoded CSV column is called and what a preset stores, so 'Road speed' logging as r53 was a name only the UI could see. 0x53 is now speed, 0x6C idle_step_pos, 0x57 run_state, 0x7A kill_run and 0x79 kill_stop, and the three presets were rewritten to match. 0x35 is 'Advance (latched)' rather than 'Advance ignition', because latching is exactly what separates it from the live 0x37 and the protocol reference already said so. 0x7A/0x79 moved to known: the pair is strictly inverse across all 261 samples where both were read, 0x7A stands at 1 in every one of the 98 running samples and flipped to 1 in the sample the starter pulled the battery to 7.9 V, and the rider confirmed the kill switch is what was being worked -- the one part that rested on memory rather than measurement. 0x57 moved with them as the run state: 4 running on 732 of 733 samples above 500 rpm, 8 after the kill button, both watched. Its third value, 16, is labelled a guess in status_maps.json -- it stood for two samples at one stop and arrived 18 s after another, which reads as the sleep the ECU announces to the bus once the ignition is gone, and a stop recorded with the ignition left on for a minute is what would settle it. The 2026-09-10 ride -- three presets across one 23-minute run, 25 -> 96 C, up to 5375 rpm -- settled nine of the nine unknown rli that had a slot of their own, and two of the digital-input block. 0x75 is the engine-running flag: it equals (0x58 != 0) in 296 of 297 samples, sets in the sample the starter pulls the battery to 10.1 V with rpm still 0, and clears in the sample the engine stops -- the same information as the engine-state bitfield, from one byte. 0x62 is the idle mode named in its own row: 0 with the engine stopped, 4 at idle (1168-2234 rpm, throttle at the 1.6-2.0 deg stop) and 2 off idle (1223-5053 rpm, throttle to 25 deg), with no overlap. 0x5C is not the closed-throttle switch it was guessed to be -- 'throttle > 2 deg' agrees on only 92 % of samples and no lag or threshold does better -- it is the flag of the correction 0x6A carries: (0x5C == 4) == (0x6A > 0) in 680 of 693 samples, and all 13 exceptions are single samples on a transition, where the two rli are read one request apart. 0x6A itself is not the 'cruise only, 0..21' it was written down as: it runs 0..29, it is non-zero only off idle -- it lifts in the very sample the throttle leaves the stop and drops to 0 when it returns -- and its level falls with the coolant: mean 23.5 at 25-34 C, 19.8 at 35-44, 17.5 at 45-54, 15.7 at 55-64, 12.3 at 65-74, 9.3 at 75-84 and 9.9 at 85-94 (r = -0.79 against coolant over its 348 non-zero samples), while inside one activation it holds rather than decaying, so it is a warm-up enrichment applied off idle and not an accelerator-pump transient. Both keep 'check': the shape is measured, the quantity behind the number is not, and a cold start held at a fixed throttle is what would name it. 0x5D/0x5E/0x5F/0x63/0x6E/0x70 held a flat 0 through the whole ride -- the rev limiter, a 25 -> 96 C warm-up and 5375 rpm -- and carry 'dead': true now. Unlike the 34 firmware stubs each of the six has a slot of its own, so that flag records a measurement rather than a property of the software: drop it and they come back. 0x74 and 0x77 (a constant 1 through cranking, running, a kill-switch stop and both switch positions) and 0x3E (a constant 52 through everything) stay selectable on purpose: a constant is not a zero, and the one state none of them has been recorded in is the ignition switched off, which is what the Sleep preset is for.

params.name: rli 0x3B (null; was “CO / duty”, CO Trimm is 0x3D)
rli 0x3E (config byte, const 52; ignition-off still untried)
